messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Q on stan_colext() in ubms
parts:
Dear all,

we're fitting some dynamic occupancy models to a 126 site x 26 year data set. Ext and col is both very low, and p is very high, so from a model with year-specific fixed effects in unmarked we get LOTS of estimates that are on the boundary (i.e., 0 or 1).

So we went to ubms instead and tried stan_colext(), which conveniently has about 99% the same syntax as colext() in unmarked, but uses the Bayesian engine Stan under the hood. We fitted the same fixed-effects model as in unmarked. This takes about 21 min on my laptop (compared to about half of that time in unmarked) and produces no boundary estimates. By taking the posterior mean rather than the mode in a Bayesian analysis one is almost guaranteed not to get them.

Attached is a plot that shows estimates vs. truth for a single simulated data set for unmarked and for ubms and then a comparison of Bayes vs. MLE. In that last plot, MLEs on the boundary can be well seen at the bottom left and the top right.

So, all of this looks quite nice, but I have two questions:
  1. We got this error message from ubms; any ideas what it means ?
Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'i' in selecting a method for function '[': argument "submodel" is missing, with no default
  1. I'd like to get an estimate of the total population size for each year, which in our case is the sum of occupied sites in every year. In unmarked I can get this by issuing this obscure command:
nocc.hat <- colSums(ranef(fm)@post[,2,])

Any chance to get this from ubms as well ?

Thanks a lot and best regards  --- Marc

messages.subject: Re: Q on stan_colext() in ubms
parts:
And then I have another one. When trying to fit a dynocc model in ubms with random effects of years, I get an error:

> summary(fmR <- stan_colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~ (1 | year),
+    epsilonformula = ~ (1 | year), pformula = ~ (1 | year),
+    data = umf, chains = 3, iter = 500))

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'colext' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'summary': cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(messages, open = "wt") :
  cannot open file 'C:\Users\marc_\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpyY0Ock\file10e416bf6725': No such file or directory

Any idea what I am doing wrong ?

Thanks and best regards  --- Marc

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Q on stan_colext() in ubms
parts:
Hi Marc,

Glad you are finding ubms useful!

For the error message in your 2nd email, can you try running the model step and the summary step separately? So

fmR <- stan_colext()
summary(fmR)

For the error message in your first email, that looks like a bug. Can you send me some small example code where you get this error message?

For your final question, ubms calculates the marginal likelihood so the latent presence/absence z in each year is not available as it is e.g. with JAGS. However ubms has the posterior_predict() function which can generate post-hoc simulated posteriors of z in a manner similar to what ranef does in unmarked. The output format may be a little unexpected, see ?posterior_predict for a description of how it is arranged.

Ken
